query: Consider the following context: The ability to endure extreme corrosion in challenging environments is reduced in stainless steel. This can be addressed by appropriate surface modification techniques to redefine the surface with the required properties. In that context, which method can be used for improved corrosion resistance, and why?

generation.hypothesis: If stainless steel surfaces undergo plasma nitriding under controlled temperature conditions, a nitrogen-enriched diffusion layer (expanded austenite) will form and significantly improve corrosion resistance in aggressive aqueous environments compared with untreated stainless steel.
generation.material_initial_state: Conventional austenitic stainless steel (e.g., 316L) with a standard mill finish.
generation.intervention: Plasma nitriding of the stainless steel surface at moderate temperatures (e.g., 400–500 °C) under controlled ammonia or nitrogen-rich atmospheres.
generation.conditions: Exposed to chloride-rich or acidic solutions at elevated temperature (e.g., 50–80 °C) for a specified duration (e.g., up to 500 hours).
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a nitrogen-enriched surface layer (S-phase or expanded austenite) that enhances passivity and reduces pitting initiation sites.
generation.mechanism: The nitrogen atoms diffuse into the steel surface lattices, creating a modified microstructure that lowers the diffusion rates of corrosive species and enhances the surface passivation layer’s stability.
generation.predicted_outcome: A measurable reduction in corrosion rates (e.g., at least 20–30% lower mass loss compared to untreated stainless steel) under the specified acidic/chloride environment.
generation.baseline: Untreated stainless steel of the same grade tested under identical conditions, serving as control for corrosion rate measurements.
generation.boundary: The enhanced corrosion resistance is most reliably observed within specific temperature and time windows for plasma nitriding; outside these parameters, non-optimal nitride phases or excessive nitrogen diffusion can reduce the protective effect.
generation.uncertainty: Quantitative magnitude of the improvement can vary with alloy composition, process temperature, and environment specifics, and no identical effect is guaranteed across all stainless steel grades.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare sets of stainless steel coupons, subject half to plasma nitriding, and compare their corrosion behavior via standardized immersion or electrochemical tests in chloride-rich solutions under controlled temperature for a fixed duration.
measurements: Mass loss of coupons after immersion
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the nitrided samples do not exhibit reduced mass loss or higher pitting potential relative to non-nitrided controls under these conditions, the hypothesis would be falsified.
